patch.summary: Retain upstream's indexed delivery fallback for unread/ACK inboxes and add complementary real-engine, snapshot, tool, and benchmark coverage
selection: Preserve upstream's single newest-header page for dense or tightly time-bounded unread/ACK reads
Page shared delivery IDs through the existing project/timestamp index after incomplete speculation
Apply direct-recipient precedence and per-viewer read/ACK state before loading fallback message headers
Retain the requested newest window using authoritative messages.created_ts and message ID
Treat delivered_ts only as a traversal key, including when imported delivery timestamps differ from message timestamps
Keep visibility, selection, receipts, and body hydration inside the existing read snapshot
patch.memory_bound: One delivery page and the requested top-N window, with bounded primary-key header lookups; no materialized project-message history
patch.scope_limit: The indexed fallback applies to unread/ACK filters and still examines shared-delivery history. Unfiltered reads retain upstream behavior. Very large equal-delivered_ts runs can require repeated traversal because the existing cursor offsets within the current boundary timestamp run.
followup_changes: Extract the existing delivery SQL unchanged so query-plan and snapshot tests observe the actual production query
Compare fixed shared-delivery populations at two unrelated-history sizes, including fully read inboxes
Check cursor seeks, cancellation at receipt/header stages, and a real peer-commit snapshot race
Exercise metadata peek, consuming reads, per-agent receipts, and direct-recipient precedence through real tools
Keep the legacy shared-merge reference on the uncapped incumbent and retain all concurrent upstream regressions
Add sparse-shared unread Criterion workloads and record validation blockers without performance claims
